key_insight: YoCausal tests whether video generation models genuinely learn causality, not just short-term visual patterns. By using real videos and their time-reversed versions as natural counterfactuals, it provides a more realistic way to probe world-model behavior.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of realistic benchmarks for evaluating whether video diffusion models understand cause-and-effect. Existing tests often rely on synthetic data, which suffers from a sim-to-real gap and may not reflect real-world generalization.
method: Introduces YoCausal, a two-level benchmark inspired by the Violation of Expectation (VoE) paradigm from cognitive science.
Constructs natural counterfactual samples by temporally reversing real-world videos at zero cost.
Evaluates whether models can distinguish plausible causal motion from impossible or reversed temporal dynamics.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and practitioners measure whether video generators are moving toward true world models or only memorizing temporal statistics. It can guide the development of more causally aware, robust video generation systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side frame sequence of a normal video versus its time-reversed counterfactual

paper_title: YoCausal: How Far is Video Generation from World Model? A Causality Perspective
paper_authors: You-Zhe Xie, Yu-Hsuan Li, Jie-Ying Lee, Kaipeng Zhang, Yu-Lun Liu
